title: On the Optimal Sample Complexity of Offline Multi-Armed Bandits with KL Regularization
abstract: arXiv:2605.02141v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization is widely used in offline decision-making and offers several benefits, motivating recent work on the sample complexity of offline learning with respect to KL-regularized performance metrics. Nevertheless, the exact sample complexity of KL-regularized offline learning remains largely from fully characterized. In this paper, we study this question in the setting of multi-armed bandits (MABs). We provide a sharp analysis of KL-PCB (Zhao et al., 2026), showing that it achieves a sample complexity of $\tilde{O}(\eta SAC^{\pi^*}/\epsilon)$ under large regularization $\eta = \tilde{O}(\epsilon^{-1})$, and a sample complexity of $\tilde{\Omega}(SAC^{\pi^*}/\epsilon^2)$ under small regularization $\eta = \tilde{\Omega}(\epsilon^{-1})$, where $\eta$ is the regularization parameter, $S$ is the number of contexts, $A$ is the number of arms, $C^{\pi^*}$ policy coverage coefficient at the optimal policy $

translated_title: 关于KL正则化离线多臂老虎机的最优样本复杂度
translated_abstract: Kullback-Leibler（KL）正则化在离线决策中被广泛使用，并具有诸多优势，这促使了近期关于基于KL正则化性能指标的离线学习样本复杂度的研究。然而，KL正则化离线学习的精确样本复杂度在很大程度上仍未被完全刻画。本文在多臂老虎机（MABs）的设置下研究这一问题。我们对KL-PCB算法（Zhao et al., 2026）进行了精确的分析，证明其在大正则化 $\eta = \tilde{O}(\epsilon^{-1})$ 下达到 $\tilde{O}(\eta SAC^{\pi^*}/\epsilon)$ 的样本复杂度，而在小正则化 $\eta = \tilde{\Omega}(\epsilon^{-1})$ 下达到 $\tilde{\Omega}(SAC^{\pi^*}/\epsilon^2)$ 的样本复杂度，其中 $\eta$ 为正则化参数，$S$ 为上下文数量，$A$ 为臂的数量，$C^{\pi^*}$ 为最优策略 $\pi^*$ 处的策略覆盖系数。
tldr: 本文在多臂老虎机设置下对KL正则化离线学习算法KL-PCB给出了精确分析，证明其在大、小正则化条件下分别达到 $\tilde{O}(\eta SAC^{\pi^*}/\epsilon)$ 和 $\tilde{\Omega}(SAC^{\pi^*}/\epsilon^2)$ 的样本复杂度，从而基本刻画了KL正则化离线学习的最优样本复杂度。
en_tdlr: This paper provides a sharp analysis of the KL-PCB algorithm for offline multi-armed bandits with KL regularization, establishing sample complexities of $\tilde{O}(\eta SAC^{\pi^*}/\epsilon)$ under large regularization and $\tilde{\Omega}(SAC^{\pi^*}/\epsilon^2)$ under small regularization, essentially characterizing the optimal sample complexity of KL-regularized offline learning.
